data.content_ref: inline:Add a compact root-validity certificate layer: for each committed root, emit a polylog-size commitment (Merkle-style hash chain over the greedy defense tree) that an external verifier can check without recomputing the fixed point. This shifts the burden from computation to verification and preserves all existing guarantees, since certificates are derived strictly post-hoc from the fixed point. Criticizable: the defense tree of an accepted node may be super-polylog in size, so the certificate is not actually polylog without compression that loses witness detail; hash-based soundness imports cryptographic assumptions foreign to the current deterministic model; certificate construction order must itself be proven canonical to avoid SRC_008-style order dependence.
